steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 9x5-inch loaf pan and set aside.
Cream together sugar and shortening. Add eggs and vanilla; beat until fluffy.

Sift together flour, oats, baking soda, salt, and cinnamon. Add dry ingredients alternately with bananas and milk to wet ingredients. Mix until blended. Fold in raisins and pour into the prepared pan.
Bake in the preheated oven for 50 to 60 minutes; remove from oven and cover for 5 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Banana Oatmeal Bread
raw_recipe.description: This banana oat bread is an old family recipe that is moist, delicious, and easy to make. This treat will become your family favorite as well.
raw_recipe.name: Banana Oatmeal Bread

review.reviewBody: 5 Stars. A wonderful, tasty bread. Used 1/2 Cup applesauce and 1/2 Cup butter in place of shortening, used 3 bananas for a moist bread, no raisins. The crust came out really well! Lovely.

Yes! I made this the other day and yes I went ahead and made a few changes... I used 1/2 light brown sugar and 1/2 white sugar. Then like some other notes I've read on banana bread, I added nutmeg and allspice with the cinnamon. Also used 1 T lemon juice to the milk. Oh and I chopped walnuts and just layered them on top of the loaf after putting it in the baking pan. That's about it. Also, I did use two large over-ripe bananas mashed. It's sweet, spicy and kind of tropical - with the crunch of the walnut topping and baked at 325 degrees because my oven runs hot! The loaf pan was placed on a foil covered cookie sheet while baking. I'm really excited about this recipe and it's adjustments give me exactly what I'm looking for in flavor! Enjoy your adjustments or not, my friends!

I used applesauce instead of shortening and only 3/4 cup sugar. Mashed 4 smaller-sized bananas and just threw it all in a big bowl and mixed together with just a fork (didn't sift together, alternate adding, etc.). Folded in chocolate chips at the end instead of the raisins because...well...why not? Good texture, great taste, easy recipe that I made with my daughter's assistance--and will be making again!

This will be my new go to when I have almost rotten banans.LOL 
Amazing texture with the oatmeal, but since you can't sift oats, I sifted the other dry ingredients together and then stirred in the oats. Also doubled the cinnamon, used butter instead of shortening and added chopped walnuts and dark chocolate chunks. AMAZING!!! I can't stop "sampling" it...HA HA

We had 5 overripe bananas to deal with, came to just over 2 cups of mashed bananas. So increased the recipe by a half -- 3 eggs, a stick and a half of butter, a cup and half each of sugar, flour, and oatmeal etc. 

Instead of all-purpose flour, used King Arthur Stone Ground Organic Whole Wheat White; instead of quick-cook oats, used Quaker old-fashioned rolled oats. Oh and 2 of the eggs were duck eggs, the third a chicken egg. Used chopped pecans instead of raisins. 

40 min, and it was cooked all the way through with just a bit of a dark crust -- it would have started to burn if we'd left it in any longer. Better than great. A recipe that tolerates many substitutions! :)

Absolutely delicious. I substitute shortening with butter as that is what I had. I also switched walnuts for raisins out of personal preference. Bread is moist, with great texture and not chewy at all. I used muffin tins and baked for 20minutes.

I use softened butter as the shortening, and be sure to beat the eggs before adding them to anything, and I use 1 1/4 C of gluten-free cup-4-cup flour instead of regular, and 1 1/2 C mashed bananas was 3 medium bananas, and I added 1/4 C chopped pecans and 1/2 cup chocolate chips instead of the raisins, and it can make 18 muffins which take 15-20 minutes to bake. The muffins freeze (and thaw) well. I am not a huge banana bread fan, and the oats (and chocolate chips and pecans) tame down the banana taste.

This banana bread came out so moist and delicious! This is the best banana bread I've made! I made this into jumbo muffins. I added about a cup of chocolate chips and 3-4 tbsp. of chia, instead of quick oats I used old fashioned oats, and used about 5 bananas . I topped the muffins with old fashioned oats and a dash of brown sugar. They came out amazing!!!

Love this recipe for banana bread. I like to add butterscotch chips or chocolate chips instead of raisins. For finishing, I brush the top with jelly (any flavor will do. Currently using lavender-violet jelly) and sprinkle rolled oats on top. If you like more crunch, add you favorite granola mix on top before cooking. Brush the top with jelly for a shiny look.
It was so good! Soaked the oats in the milk as somebody suggested and added frozen blueberries that I had rolled in flour. Also replaced the shortening with butter. Will definitely make again!

This bread is awesome! I didn’t have shortening so the first time I used 1/2 veg oil and 1/2 unsweetened applesauce. Also, used 2/3c brown sugar. Today I used 1/2c brown sugar and mistakenly used 1/2c of unsweetened applesauce so I skipped the oil. Wasn’t sure what would happen. Was plenty moist so I skipped the milk. Still awesome! Upped the cinnamon too. I make 3 mini loaves and freeze the others. So darn good!
I added cranberries to it and omitted the raisins
I substituted butter for oil and added peanuts, cranberries and raisins. Came out beautiful and soft.
I used King Arthur Gluten Free Measure For Measure Flour in this and the result was AMAZING. Best gluten free recipe I have ever made!
I do this recipe often, but without wheat. I substitute rice flour for 1/2 cup wheat .
Great recipe. Used canola oil. Replaced sugar with half monk fruit and dark brown sugar.
My “go to” banana bread base recipe. Moist and delicious!
Substituted 1cup sugar for 1/4cup honey + 1/4cup brown sugar, instead of shortening I used applesauce Crushed walnut pieces and caramel chips were added as well
I doubled this recipe. As with most banana breads I added and extra 1/2 cup more bananas, I also added chocolate chips and walnuts. My family loved it.
